s: Which Andhra dynasty issued iron coins with thin copper coating?
x:
The Shalankayanas were unique among the early Andhra dynasties for issuing iron coins coated with a thin layer of copper. This distinctive coinage is an important feature that helps historians identify the dynasty archaeologically. The Shalankayanas ruled the Vengi region between the 4th and 5th centuries CE after the decline of the Ikshvakus. Their coins reflect both economic conditions and technological practices of the period. Unlike the Shalankayanas, the Satavahanas predominantly issued lead, copper, potin and silver coins, while the Ikshvakus and Vishnukundins mainly issued copper coins.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (3).
n: Distinctive Coin – Iron coin with thin copper coating

s: 'Janasraya' is the title of which of the following Vishnukundin rulers?
x: The Vishnukundins were one of the most powerful dynasties of early medieval Andhra Pradesh. Among their rulers, Madhavavarma II was the greatest and assumed the title Janasraya, meaning "Refuge of the People." Madhavavarma II significantly expanded the kingdom, strengthened the administration and performed several Vedic sacrifices, including the Ashvamedha. His reign marked the political zenith of the Vishnukundin dynasty. The famous work Janasraya Chandas, a treatise on Sanskrit prosody, is traditionally associated with his reign.
n: Capital shifted to Denduluru during Madhavavarma II
